newsitem.title: UK: Eramet targets over 60,000 T nickel output by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Eramet targets over 60,000 T nickel output by 2000.

text.p: French nickel group Eramet plans to produce over 60,000 tonnes of nickel by 2000, up 13 percent from expected 1996 output of 53,000 tonnes, chairman Yves Rambaud said on Thursday.
The eventual figure could be higher, he added.
"We see a production figure in the range of 60,000 to 65,000 tonnes at the beginning of the next century," he told a presentation to the Association of Mining Analysts.
Rambaud said higher output would come from its nickel facilities in New Caledonia, where the company recently decided to build a fifth rotary kiln at its Doniambo smelter.
Preliminary work also continues on the Tiebaghi nickel deposit, he added.
Rambaud said production was already on the rise during the first half of this year, with 26,280 tonnes produced during the first six months, up three percent from year-ago levels.

Sales were also higher at 27,342 tonnes, up five percent from the 26,129 tonnes delivered during the first half of 1995. This was despite lower global nickel consumption due to lower stainless steel output.
Stainless steel accounts for two thirds of nickel demand.
The main area of growth for sales was in Asia, accounting for 40 percent of Eramet's deliveries in the first half.

"We sold more nickel in Asia for the first time than in Europe," Rambaud said. Rambaud warned that lower nickel prices during the third quarter of the year could have an important impact on the group's full-year results.

"The fall (in prices) during the third quarter will have an impact on (our selling) prices during the third and fourth quarters (of 1996), whathever happens during October, November and December," Rambaud said.
"For nickel, deliveries will certainly be above those in 1995 and prices will certainly be below those of 1995," he said.
In the group's other main sector, high speed steels, Rambaud said in 1996 Eramet's deliveries would "clearly be lower than 1995", while prices would be equal or above those of last year.
During the first half of 1996 Rambaud said the group's high speed steel deliveries fell eight percent to 14,374 tonnes.
But this partly reflected the overall economic slowdown in Europe and Japan and destocking by tool manufacturers.
The company maintained its share of the world market (excluding the former Soviet Union and China) at 30 percent.
Last week Eramet reported net attributable profits for the six month to end-June of 167 million French francs from 174 million during the year-ago period.
